transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I’m not sure how to explain it properly. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but lately when I’m walking across campus, I get this really unsettling feeling like I’m seeing everything through glass. Like I’m there, but not completely in my own body, and the buildings and students around me feel… a little unreal. It’s been scaring me, honestly.
Do you ever feel detached from yourself, like you're watching yourself from outside your body, or feel like your surroundings aren't real?

Yes… I mean, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but what scares me most is when I’m walking across campus and it feels like I’m seeing everything through glass. Like I’m there, but not quite fully in my own body. The buildings and the students around me feel sort of… unreal, or distant. Does that make sense?
Do you experience these feelings of detachment or unreality in other situations, or does it only happen when you're walking across campus?

Mostly when I’m walking across campus, I think. That’s when I notice it the most, anyway. It’s like I’m looking at everything through glass, and I’m not completely in my body… and the buildings and people around me feel a bit unreal. I don’t know if that’s the right way to say it.
Do you ever feel this sense of detachment or unreality in situations other than when you're walking across campus, like while you're at home, in class, or during other activities?

I think it’s mostly the campus walks, yes. I don’t notice it as much at home or when I’m just sitting somewhere… or maybe I’m better at ignoring it then. But the thing that really frightens me is being out there and suddenly feeling like I’m watching everything through glass, like I’m not quite in my own body and the buildings and students don’t feel completely real. I’m sorry if I’m repeating myself — that’s just the clearest way I can describe it.
Have you ever felt this same sense of being detached or things feeling unreal in situations other than walking across campus, like when you're in class, at home, or talking with friends?

I’m not sure I’d say it happens the same way in class or at home. Maybe little moments, but the one I really notice—and the one that scares me—is walking across campus. It’s like there’s glass between me and everything, and I’m not fully in my body. The buildings and students feel just a little unreal. I hope that answers what you’re asking.

Have you ever noticed even mild feelings of being detached from yourself or things feeling unreal, even if not as intense as when you're walking across campus, during other everyday activities like talking to someone, reading, or watching TV?

Maybe a little, but… I don’t think it’s as clear when I’m reading or watching TV or talking to someone. I might feel kind of distant for a second, but I’m not sure I’d want to make too much of that.

The part that really scares me is still when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it feels like I’m seeing everything through glass, and I’m not quite fully in my body, and the buildings and students around me seem slightly unreal. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Can you think of any time when you've felt even slightly detached from yourself or like things around you weren't quite real, even for just a moment, while doing something like talking to a friend, reading, or watching a lecture?

Maybe… very briefly, yes, but it’s hard for me to say if it’s the same thing. I don’t want to overstate it.

The clearest one is still when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it scares me—like I’m seeing everyone and the buildings through glass, and I’m not quite fully inside my own body. Everything feels just a little unreal for a moment. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?

Can you recall any specific moment—like during a conversation, while reading, or sitting quietly—when you briefly felt even slightly detached from yourself or like your surroundings were a little unreal, even if not as intense as when you’re walking across campus?

I’m sorry, I know I keep coming back to the same example. I can’t really pin down a specific time during a conversation or reading where I’d confidently say it happened.

The moment I can describe is when I’m walking across campus. That’s when it scares me—like I’m watching everything through glass, and I don’t feel fully in my own body. The buildings and students around me seem just a little unreal. I’m not sure if that’s enough of an answer, but that’s the clearest one.

Can you think of any time—maybe during a quiet moment alone or while doing something routine—when you felt even the slightest sense of being detached from yourself or like things around you felt a bit unreal, even if just for a few seconds?

I’m sorry, I know I may not be answering this exactly the way you’re asking. The example I keep coming back to is walking across campus. That’s when it’s most noticeable and, honestly, the part that scares me.

It’s like I’m seeing everything through glass for a moment—like I’m not fully in my own body, and the buildings and students around me feel a little unreal. Maybe it only lasts briefly, but it feels very strange. I’m not sure if that counts as what you mean.

I’m sorry, I know I’m repeating myself a bit. I can’t really think of a clear example sitting quietly or before falling asleep.
